texte.arena-sand.info: A round sand pit with a stone ring and three rows of planks. Men walk in through the gate; how many walk out is up to the gods and the crowd.
texte.arena-sand.name: Arena
texte.baum-apfel.info: Red apples, free for the taking. The worms were here first and they are not sharing.
texte.baum-apfel.name: Apple Tree
texte.baum-birke.info: A pale birch. Its rods are flexible, cheap and well remembered by every recruit.
texte.baum-birke.name: Birch
texte.baum-buche.info: A broad beech with a smooth grey trunk. Burns long and hot, which the smith appreciates more than the beech does.
texte.baum-buche.name: Beech
texte.baum-eiche-skizze.info: An oak older than the empire and twice as honest. Its roots have drunk from more battlefields than any legionary. Excellent shade, terrible witness.
texte.baum-eiche-skizze.name: Old Oak
texte.baum-pappel.info: A tall, thin poplar. Soft wood, fast growth and no character at all, rather like a senator.
texte.baum-pappel.name: Poplar
texte.baum-tanne.info: A dark fir, straight as a spear. Makes good beams, good masts and, if business is slow, good coffins.
texte.baum-tanne.name: Fir
texte.bett-stroh.info: A wooden frame, old straw and one blanket. The fleas were here first and they pay no rent either.
texte.bett-stroh.name: Straw Bed
texte.bk-feld.info: Furrows of dark earth with green shoots. Somebody sweated here so somebody else can eat in the stands.
texte.bk-feld.name: Ploughed Field
texte.bk-lehm-boden.info: Stamped clay with straw in it. Spill something and it becomes part of the floor.
texte.bk-lehm-boden.name: Mud-and-Timber Floor
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-i.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-i.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Right
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-ab-j.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Front
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-i.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-i.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Left
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-j.info: Bundled straw over rafters. It keeps out most of the rain and none of the mice.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-auf-j.name: Thatched Roof Slope, Rear
texte.bk-lehm-dach-flach.info: A flat bed of thatch. Good for drying fish and hiding from tax men.
texte.bk-lehm-dach-flach.name: Thatched Roof, Flat
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-ab.info: The other half of the timber gable. Nobody remembers which half was built first.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-ab.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-auf.info: The pointed end of a timber gable. The birds nest here and pay no rent.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel-auf.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-lehm-giebel.info: Boards nailed up under the end of the roof. They hold, mostly.
texte.bk-lehm-giebel.name: Mud-and-Timber Gable
texte.bk-lehm-rang.info: Rows of plank benches. Splinters are free and so is the view of the killing.
texte.bk-lehm-rang.name: Mud-and-Timber Tiers
texte.bk-lehm-schild.info: A crooked board on a stick with a daub of paint. Nobody can read, so a picture of a sausage does the job.
texte.bk-lehm-schild.name: Mud-and-Timber Sign
texte.bk-lehm-tuer.info: A plank door that sticks in summer and in winter. In spring it merely creaks.
texte.bk-lehm-tuer.name: Mud-and-Timber Door
texte.bk-lehm-wand.info: Clay packed over a timber frame. Cracks come free of charge, draughts are included.
texte.bk-lehm-wand.name: Mud-and-Timber Wall
texte.bk-marmor-boden.info: Marble slabs with a purple inlay. Slippery when wet, and it is always wet with something.
texte.bk-marmor-boden.name: Marble Floor
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i.info: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-i.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Right
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j.info: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-ab-j.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Front
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-i.info: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-i.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Left
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-j.info: Thin marble slabs with gilded seams. Nobody needs a marble roof, which is exactly why it is bought.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-auf-j.name: Marble-Slab Roof Slope, Rear
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach.info: Flat marble slabs on top. Ideal for a terrace and for looking down on the street.
texte.bk-marmor-dach-flach.name: Marble-Slab Roof, Flat
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-ab.info: The other gilded pediment edge. Symmetry costs extra and the owner paid.
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-ab.name: Marble Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-auf.info: A gilded pediment edge. The gods look down from here, the owner looks down on everyone else.
texte.bk-marmor-giebel-auf.name: Marble Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-marmor-giebel.info: A marble gable, straight as a senator claims to be.
texte.bk-marmor-giebel.name: Marble Gable
texte.bk-marmor-rang.info: White marble tiers for people who never sit on anything cheaper. The blood looks better from here.
texte.bk-marmor-rang.name: Marble Tiers
texte.bk-marmor-schild.info: A bronze plaque on a marble pedestal. Whatever it advertises, you cannot afford it.
texte.bk-marmor-schild.name: Marble Sign
texte.bk-marmor-tuer.info: A bronze door with gilded studs. Heavy enough to keep out the mob and, on a good day, the creditors.
texte.bk-marmor-tuer.name: Marble Door
texte.bk-marmor-wand.info: Polished marble with a gilded band, paid for with somebody else's blood. Marble always is.
texte.bk-marmor-wand.name: Marble Wall
texte.bk-ziegel-boden.info: Terracotta tiles, red and buff. They hide wine stains well and blood even better.
texte.bk-ziegel-boden.name: Brick Floor
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-i.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Right
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-ab-j.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Front
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-i.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Left
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j.info: Red clay tiles in neat rows. One loose tile per storm, one dead passer-by per decade.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-auf-j.name: Tiled Roof Slope, Rear
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach.info: A flat tiled roof. In summer the family sleeps up here, in winter the cat.
texte.bk-ziegel-dach-flach.name: Tiled Roof, Flat
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-ab.info: The falling half of a plastered gable. Rain runs down it and into the neighbour's window.
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-ab.name: Brick Gable Peak (down)
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-auf.info: The peak of a plastered gable. The highest point of the house and of the landlord's ambitions.
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel-auf.name: Brick Gable Peak (up)
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel.info: A plastered gable wall. Pigeons rent it by the day.
texte.bk-ziegel-giebel.name: Brick Gable
texte.bk-ziegel-rang.info: Tiers of stone seats. Bring a cushion, or rent one at a price that hurts more than the stone.
texte.bk-ziegel-rang.name: Brick Tiers
texte.bk-ziegel-schild.info: A painted signboard with a red frame. It promises quality and is right about half the time.
texte.bk-ziegel-schild.name: Brick Sign
texte.bk-ziegel-tuer.info: A wooden door under a brick lintel. Knock twice; the third knock is always the debt collector.
texte.bk-ziegel-tuer.name: Brick Door
texte.bk-ziegel-wand.info: Plastered brick on a red plinth. Respectable enough to have debts.
texte.bk-ziegel-wand.name: Brick Wall
texte.blume-distel.info: A thistle with a purple crown. It stabs everyone who touches it and has never lost a fight.
texte.blume-distel.name: Thistle
texte.blume-schilf.info: Reeds at the edge of the water. Good for roofs, baskets and for losing a sandal.
texte.blume-schilf.name: Reeds
texte.blume-wiese.info: A handful of wildflowers. Pretty, harmless and trampled within the week.
texte.blume-wiese.name: Wildflowers
texte.boden-erde.info: Honest dirt with a few pebbles. Everything you own will end up in it, and so will you.
texte.boden-erde.name: Bare Earth
texte.boden-fels.info: Solid rock. Nothing grows here and nothing can be buried here, which makes it popular with neither farmers nor undertakers.
texte.boden-fels.name: Bedrock
texte.boden-gras.info: Grass. It grows on anything, including last season's losers.
texte.boden-gras.name: Grass
texte.boden-sand.info: Fine sand, excellent at soaking up whatever gets spilled on it. The arena uses the same kind, for the same reason.
texte.boden-sand.name: Sand
texte.boden-wasser.info: Fresh water, more or less. The men drink from it, the oxen stand in it, and nobody asks in which order.
texte.boden-wasser.name: Waterhole
texte.boden-weg.info: Packed earth with two cart ruts. Carts love it; whoever falls asleep on it will not love the carts.
texte.boden-weg.name: Dirt Road
texte.busch-bluete.info: A bush with orange blossoms. The bees adore it; the men use it for something less poetic.
texte.busch-bluete.name: Flowering Bush
texte.busch-gruen.info: A plain green bush. Just big enough to hide a coward, as several have already discovered.
texte.busch-gruen.name: Bush
texte.busch-hasel.info: A hazel shrub. Nuts in autumn, switches all year round.
texte.busch-hasel.name: Hazel
texte.dach-ziegel.info: Red clay tiles over a plastered gable. Keeps the rain off the men and the men out of sight.
texte.dach-ziegel.name: Tiled Roof
texte.fels-block.info: A grey boulder that has not moved since the gods dropped it. Patient, silent and completely useless until someone brings a pickaxe.
texte.fels-block.name: Boulder
texte.figur-arbeiter.info: An ordinary man of the ludus in a simple tunic. He carries, saws and digs until the day somebody hands him a sword instead.
texte.figur-arbeiter.name: Worker
texte.karren-ochse.info: A cart with one ox and three sacks. The ox does the work and the driver takes the credit; the ox is used to it.
texte.karren-ochse.name: Ox Cart
texte.lager-platz.info: A pallet with crates and a sack. Everything here belongs to somebody, and that somebody is not the man carrying it.
texte.lager-platz.name: Storage Spot
texte.leiche.info: A fallen gladiator in a dark puddle. He lies here for a day so the next ones know what the purse costs; then the cart takes him.
texte.leiche.name: Corpse
texte.markt-stand.info: The slave trader's stall. Every morning he brings five new men in chains; whoever is left at dusk goes back on the road with him. No refunds.
texte.markt-stand.name: Slave Market
texte.medicus.info: A small house with a slate roof and the staff of Asclepius over the door. The medicus sews, sets and saws for gold; the cheaper the treatment, the longer the scream.
texte.medicus.name: Medicus
texte.natur-stumpf.info: What is left of a tree after the woodcutter has been by. Give it a few days and it will try again; trees never learn.
texte.natur-stumpf.name: Tree Stump
texte.tier-reh.info: A roe deer, all eyes and nerves. It grazes, it listens, and it has no idea there is a kitchen in its future.
texte.tier-reh.name: Roe Deer
texte.wand-stein.info: A wall of cut stone with moss at its foot. Keeps the weather out and the workforce in.
texte.wand-stein.name: Stone Wall
texte.wand-tor.info: A double gate with bronze bands, wide enough for an ox cart. It opens for deliveries and closes for second thoughts.
texte.wand-tor.name: Gate
texte.wand-tuer.info: A plank door with a bronze handle, wide enough for one man. Carts, oxen and big ideas have to use the gate.
texte.wand-tuer.name: Door
texte.ware-bretter.info: A neat stack of sawn planks. Today a workshop wall, tomorrow perhaps a lid.
texte.ware-bretter.name: Planks
texte.ware-fleisch.info: A fresh haunch on a board. Best not to ask which animal, as long as it was an animal.
texte.ware-fleisch.name: Meat
texte.ware-stamm.info: Three trimmed logs, stacked. Heavy, splintery and always needed somewhere uphill.
texte.ware-stamm.name: Logs
texte.werk-bank.info: A sturdy bench with an anvil and a hammer. Planks, tools and the occasional fingertip are made here.
texte.werk-bank.name: Workbench
